# Welcome

## USGOVT101

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 44px;"}
By the end of this course you will be able to explain how the American constitutional system tries to let dignified equals live together with as little organized violence as possible.
:::

## Who this course is for

- Students in an introductory U.S. government or U.S. constitution course
- Independent learners
- Anyone who wants a serious, institution-agnostic treatment of the American system

This version is not tied to any college, LMS, or commercial textbook platform.

# The problem this course is about

## The core problem

How to live together peacefully in a society of dignified equals.

## Working definition of government

Government is the organization whose use of organized coercive force is widely treated as legitimate.

## Why limit government

- Government limits criminal and foreign violence — and is itself coercive force.
- Humans are not omniscient. Trade-offs and unintended consequences are normal.
- Counter-majoritarian rules exist so losers of elections still have rights and a chance to win next time.

# How the course works

## Lectures, readings, and outside sources

- The lecture is not a substitute for a textbook.
- A textbook is not a substitute for the lecture.
- Neither replaces assigned outside readings.
- Outside readings are first-class materials.

- The Declaration of Independence
- The Constitution of the United States, including the Bill of Rights
- Federalist Nos. 10 and 51
- Brutus I
